newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Safras sees Brazil 97/98 soy crop at 27.6 mln tns.
newsitem.headline: Safras sees Brazil 97/98 soy crop at 27.6 mln tns.

text.p: Brazil's soybean harvest could hit a record 27.6 million tonnes in 1997/98 as high prices fuel planting and new export corridors favour soybean growing in remoter areas, independent consultant Safras e Mercado said.

"The first signs for the planting of the new soybean harvest in Brazil are effectively positive and should be reflected in a renewed increase in the area planted from September onwards," Safras said in a weekly report.
Planted area should rise five percent on 1996/97, reaching a total of 12 million hectares.
"With an average productivity of 2,300 kilos per hectare, the new harvest would reach close to 27.6 million tonnes, representing a new record for Brazil," Safras said.

The agency revised down its forecast for the 1996/97 harvest to 26.02 million tonnes from its most recent estimate of 26.22 million tonnes, mainly due to drought in the key growing area of Rio Grande do Sul.
